clue.text: Hasn't YMCA changed the guy in the sailor outfit?

definitions.text: the guy in the sailor outfit

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the two words before it are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A nod to the Village People, whose YMCA line-up included a man dressed as a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in Hasn't is ignored; its letters H, A, S, N, T join Y, M, C, A as the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sails a yacht is a sailor, and the outfit framing nods to the pop group's costume.

clue.text: One for you experienced solvers (just the top ones)

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of each word is its first letter, and only those are kept

explanation.surface: A friendly aside picking out the seasoned solvers among the readers.
explanation.walkthrough: One for is the definition: a vote in favour is an affirmative reply.
explanation.definitionFit: An affirmative vote, counted among the ayes, is a vote cast in favour.

clue.text: Editor about to have whip round for trainee

indicators.note: round says the whip goes around the turned editor

parts.note: a cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip

indicators.note: about here means the editor's abbreviation is turned around

explanation.surface: An editor is about to pass the hat round for a junior colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip round' looks like a collection of money, but 'round' is a containment signal and 'about' turns the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person in training for the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Ditch books about American leader? That's incisive

parts.note: a trench is a ditch

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A cutting remark about ditching books on an American leader.
explanation.walkthrough: That's is a link pointing to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant comments are sharp and cutting, which is what incisive means.

clue.text: Confrère of Whistler's mother upset English model cuddling son

parts.note: MA is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the following letters upside down, so they read backwards
cuddling means the English-and-model pair wraps around the son

parts.note: to sit is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: Whistler's Mother, the famous painting, upset because an English model is cuddling her boy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Whistler's mother' as the painting, but the possessive belongs to the definition. 'Upset' reverses ESSIT into TISSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a painter, a fellow artist of James McNeill Whistler.

clue.text: To edge into traffic abroad, hooter's needed first

indicators.note: needed first puts the hooter piece ahead of the abroad piece, though the clue gives it later

parts.note: hooter is slang for the nose
abroad can mean out and about, outside

explanation.surface: Advice for a driver abroad: lead with the horn before pulling into traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooter suggests a car horn but is slang for a nose; 'needed first' sets it before the abroad piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver noses out by inching the car forward into the flow of vehicles.

clue.text: Don't go and whip on Eric's bottom

indicators.note: in an across clue, whip on Eric's bottom means the whip piece follows the bottom letter
the bottom of a word is its last letter

parts.note: to lash is to whip

explanation.surface: A stern warning not to leave and smack Eric's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Don't go is the definition: colours that clash do not go together.
explanation.definitionFit: Colours or patterns that clash are said not to go with each other, the idiom for mismatching.

clue.text: Blimey, that won't be finished for a little bit

indicators.note: the exclamation loses its last letter, so it is not finished

parts.note: crumbs is a mild exclamation of surprise, like blimey

explanation.surface: Someone exclaiming at a task too big to complete.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumb is a tiny fragment, typically of bread or cake.

clue.text: Wild sailor with individual dancing at the front

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
and means along with
one is a single individual

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sailor and a partner leading the dance with wild abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned behaviour is unrestrained and uninhibited, as wild behaviour is.

clue.text: Room heir had to get refurbished for pile

indicators.note: refurbished means remade, so the letters of the three words are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: An heir has a room done up, presumably in a big pile of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: Pile looks like a stately home in the room-and-heir picture, but here it is the medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Piles is the everyday name for swollen veins in the anus, so a pile is one of them.

clue.text: Most blue films, in the end, set dad off

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
off means gone wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dirty films eventually put Dad off.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue suggests smutty from the films, but it is sad here.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means sad, so the most blue is the most unhappy.

clue.text: Herb-covered Australian hot dog?

indicators.note: covered means the herb goes around the Australian abbreviation

parts.note: sage is a herb
AUS is a standard abbreviation for Australian

explanation.surface: An Australian hot dog topped with herbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot dog is a frankfurter in a roll, so the meat inside is a kind of banger.

clue.text: Dry ice mostly needs to go on the far side of a room

indicators.text: to go on the far side of
indicators.note: says the dry and ice pieces come after the a

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

explanation.surface: Instructions for where to put the dry ice in a room.
explanation.walkthrough: Dry suggests dry ice, but Dry alone gives TT, teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is a room in the roof space of a house.

clue.text: An old ambition crushed can be a terrible thing

indicators.note: crushed means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A long-held dream crushed is a sad affair.
explanation.definitionFit: An abomination is something loathsome or dreadful.

clue.text: Clue in Bow and the dog who might solve it?

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang, spoken in Bow in east London, clue becomes the cartoon dog's name

definitions.text: the dog who might solve it?
definitions.meaning: the Great Dane of the cartoon series solves mysteries with his friends

explanation.surface: A crossword joke: the cartoon detective dog could crack the clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of east London, home of Cockneys; 'haven't a Scooby' means having no idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang turns clue into the name of a cartoon Great Dane, who also solves mysteries.

clue.text: High-brow music, Ted? Cut and run!

parts.note: opera is classical, high-brow music

indicators.note: cut means the name loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks Ted about opera, then tells him to leg it.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut and run reads as a phrase, but Cut trims Ted and run alone is the definition; the answer also hints at the surgeon's cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate a machine or a business is to run it.

clue.text: Mysterious giant mice in another dimension!

indicators.note: moving the words into another dimension changes their form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sci-fi B-movie of giant mice from another dimension.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmatic means puzzling and hard to understand.

clue.text: Coach commercial won't feature line outside of Norway

indicators.note: the line letter is dropped and something else stands in its place

parts.note: a trailer is an advert for a film

indicators.note: the outside, front edge of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A coach-company advert that leaves out a route going beyond Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: Coach looks like a bus in the travel picture, but it means a sports trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer coaches athletes or a team.

clue.text: A new sparkling wine to drink when with a Russian princess

indicators.note: to drink means the wine takes in the following letters

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Fizz to toast a Russian royal.
explanation.walkthrough: The wine is the drinker here, not the thing drunk: 'to drink' makes it swallow the 'when' piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Anastasia was the youngest daughter of the last Tsar, a Russian grand duchess.

clue.text: Hoskins would moon jerk displaying signs of stupidity

parts.note: Hoskins is the setter, so the setter would becomes I'd
Io is a moon of Jupiter
a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: The setter admits they would happily moon at some jerk.
explanation.walkthrough: Moon and jerk look like verbs of rude behaviour, but they are nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic behaviour shows a lack of sense.

clue.text: Fancy tea during which Hoskins is sat with Her Maj

indicators.note: during which says the following pieces sit inside the tea

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
Hoskins is the setter, so the setter is becomes I'm
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: The setter enjoys a posh tea seated next to the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Fancy looks like an adjective for the tea; it is the noun, a flight of imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a wild fancy, an illusion or fantasy of the mind.

clue.text: What's-his-name is a right pain in the behind

definitions.meaning: a stand-in for someone whose name is forgotten

definitions.text: a right pain in the behind
definitions.meaning: an irritating person, a euphemism for a stronger word

explanation.surface: A grumble about someone whose name escapes the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase serves both as a placeholder for an unnamed person and as a polite insult.

clue.text: Lads holding English pub up? Call for help!

indicators.note: holding says the distress call contains the reversed English pub

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Lads propping up a bar need rescuing.
explanation.walkthrough: Holding up reads as robbery, but up reverses EINN to NNIE inside SOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonny is a familiar address for a boy, so sonnies are young lads.

clue.text: One might say: "Son, I'm said to get drunk"

definitions.note: a noun phrase here: something one might say

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A parent confesses to their son that they are said to get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted words are themselves a confession, the sort of thing the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A confession owning up to something is a statement someone might make.

clue.text: With love on the rise, kisses a couple of Carols?

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means moving up, so the round letter climbs one place

parts.note: snogs are kisses, British slang
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Romance blossoming with kisses between two women called Carol.
explanation.walkthrough: Snog is British slang for a passionate kiss. Carols are seasonal songs, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Carols are Christmas hymns, so two of them are a pair of pieces of music for singing.

clue.text: Pulled Toby half-cut, then married

indicators.note: half-cut means the name is cut in half, keeping its first half

parts.note: wed means married

explanation.surface: Toby got drunk, then tied the knot.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for drunk, but here it halves Toby. Pulled hints at a romantic conquest; it means towed.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle that is towed is hauled along behind another.

clue.text: Starters of whelks in diner excellent, nice spread

indicators.note: a starter of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A restaurant review praising a fine seafood spread of whelks.
explanation.walkthrough: Starters and spread suggest a menu; spread is a verb, to broaden.
explanation.definitionFit: To widen something is to spread it out and make it broader.

clue.text: Strong perfume making leading conservative go for model-type

indicators.note: go for means one letter leaves and is swapped for another

parts.note: incense is a perfume given off by burning

indicators.note: the leading letter of a word is its first

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car, so the model type is T

explanation.surface: A Tory leader swaps their heavy scent for something a model would wear.
explanation.definitionFit: An intense feeling or flavour is powerful and concentrated.

clue.text: One of us at home is turning ruddy contrary

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: turning means the little word is read backwards
contrary means the colour is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ruddy means red in colour

explanation.surface: Someone at home is getting red in the face and awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruddy suggests the British mild swear word, but it means red.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider belongs to the inner circle, a member of the group.

clue.text: Free travel (as long as not heading to England)

indicators.note: the journey does not go to England, so its abbreviation is dropped

parts.note: to ride is to travel

explanation.surface: Free travel, provided you are not bound for England.
explanation.walkthrough: Free looks like free of charge, but it is the verb, to rid.
explanation.definitionFit: To rid is to clear or release someone of a burden.

clue.text: Drinks fast and kisses amorously

definitions.meaning: to drink something down quickly, British slang
to kiss and cuddle, British slang

explanation.surface: A night out: downing drinks and smooching.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word both for gulping a drink and for passionate canoodling.

clue.text: Didn't drink, having retired without disgrace

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the bed word goes around the disgrace

parts.note: abed means in bed, having retired for the night
a stain is a disgrace on one's character

explanation.surface: Someone who went to bed sober with a clean record.
explanation.walkthrough: Without seems to mean lacking, but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain, especially from alcohol.
